issue.title: Telegram inbound hardening: stale-code receiver survives upgrades, offsets advance past failures, false success, unbounded retries
issue.description:
Found by the sase-zr landing audit (sase-zr note #2, gaps 9 and 10) and detailed in phases telegram-actions and telegram-receiver of the rejected completion plan (plan:202609/sase_zr_completion.md). Deliberately deferred out of the narrowed sase-zr close-out epic by owner decision on 2026-09-16: Telegram acknowledgement latency is currently acceptable, but these robustness defects remain. (Update authentication, requires_tty pre-rejection, and source tagging are NOT deferred - they land in that epic's telegram-auth phase.)

Deferred defects, all in sase-telegram:
1. Receiver never restarts after a package upgrade (no code-identity stamp; the ensure step never retires a stale receiver). This class of failure already bit us 2026-09-13 when the receiver was dead for ~a day.
2. ensure_receiver_running runs last in the job tick, so an earlier exception skips it; crash loops and stale heartbeats get no backoff and no re-alert after dismissal; the unmocked real-executable argv regression test was replaced by a mocked one in ab9d985.
3. The getUpdates offset advances before handlers durably claim updates, so a transient store error drops a button press; no durable inbox, no poison-update handling; a chat-id change starts a second consumer.
4. _send_ready_gate_completions reports success as soon as response.json exists, even if apply_side_effects later fails; acceptance-time errors (partial_attempt, gate_decision_conflict, tty_required) surface only as "background proc exited (error)"; no retry/resume/restart/cancel keyboard after failures; keyboard-cleanup tombstones and orphaned completion records retry forever on permanent errors.

task_type_fields.impact: Silent stale-code receivers after every upgrade, dropped or falsely-confirmed gate answers, no recovery affordance from Telegram after a failed attempt, and unbounded retry churn in the inbound job.
task_type_fields.repro: Examples: (a) upgrade the sase-telegram package while a receiver runs - the old-code receiver keeps running indefinitely; (b) kill the receiver between offset save and handler completion - the update is dropped; (c) make apply_side_effects fail after response.json is written and answer from Telegram - success is still reported; (d) delete the keyboard message then let cleanup run - the tombstone retries forever on BadRequest.

payload.entry: Scope evidence (sase-11y.11 land agent, 2026-09-21): defect 1 (the receiver never restarts after a package upgrade) looks addressed by sase-telegram 95354bc (0.4.18, 2026-09-19). The receiver fingerprints its runtime generation (receiver_runtime.py) and re-execs the canonical argv when the generation changes, under both the legacy durable-proc path and the service-host restart:on-failure proc (docs/inbound.md 'Long-Poll Receiver'). Three docs still tell operators that, until sase-11w lands, an upgrade needs a manual receiver restart: sase-telegram README.md:196-197 and docs/inbound.md:40-41 (4d20559, sase-zr.7.5), and sase docs/notifications.md in the Telegram receiver paragraph (420d72bb1, sase-11y.11.3, which copied that caveat). The next worker should confirm defect 1 is fixed live, drop it from this task's scope, and correct those three sentences in the same change.
